elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer must be able to terminate on 30 days' prior notice.
Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly requires written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for the period after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires Vendor to refund on a pro-rata basis all prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly states that Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
Section 9.4 expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice period must be between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is 30 days, not a period within the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 imposes no early-termination fee, so the condition requiring a cap if such a fee applies is satisfied.
Section 9.4 does not affirmatively grant Vendor a convenience-termination right; it only prohibits such termination during a committed term.

elements.element: Vendor's convenience-termination right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause bars Vendor termination during a committed term but does not expressly limit any permitted Vendor termination to the term-end date.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice requirement applies to any Vendor convenience termination.

result.reason: The redline cleanly adds every component of the preferred position while leaving the existing cause-based termination rights unchanged. It is limited to the requested convenience-termination mechanics and introduces no apparent contradiction. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its 60–90-day Customer notice period and its Vendor term-end/90-day notice framework are absent.
